Typed bounded channels and batch channels.

## Types

### `Batch`

```lang
pub extern type Batch<T>
```

A leased, sealed batch of messages; release it when processed.

#### `Batch.items`

```lang
fn items(self: &Self) -> Seq<T>
```

The batch's messages, in producer order.

#### `Batch.len`

```lang
fn len(self: &Self) -> Int
```

#### `Batch.release`

```lang
fn release(self: Self) -> Unit
```

End the lease (consuming it): the page returns to the pool. A lease
still held when its task finishes is released then.

### `BatchEndpoints`

```lang
pub type BatchEndpoints<T> = { sender: BatchSender<T>, receiver: BatchReceiver<T> }
```

### `BatchOptions`

```lang
pub type BatchOptions = { capacity: Int, max_batch: Int, byte_budget: Int }
```

### `BatchPolicy`

```lang
pub type BatchPolicy = { discard_on_close: Bool, flush_latency: Duration }
```

Batch disposal and publication policy. `discard_on_close`: staged
messages are released instead of published when the channel closes.
`flush_latency`: staged messages are published at the next safe point
once they are this old.

### `ReplyEndpoints`

```lang

```

### `ReplyReceiver`

```lang
pub extern type ReplyReceiver<T>
```

The receiving half of a one-shot reply.

#### `ReplyReceiver.recv`

```lang

```

Wait for the reply: `none` if the sender closed without one (or it
was received already).

### `ReplySender`

```lang
pub extern type ReplySender<T>
```

The sending half of a one-shot reply: one value, once.

#### `ReplySender.close`

```lang
fn close(self: &Self) -> Unit
```

Answer with nothing: the receiver's `recv` returns `none`.

#### `ReplySender.send`

```lang
fn send(self: &Self, value: T) -> Result<Unit, SendError<T>>
```

Send the reply (once; a second send, or one after `close`, is an error).

### `Selected`

```lang
enum Selected<T> { received(index: Int, value: Option<T>), sent(index: Int), closed(index: Int), too_large(index: Int), timeout }
```

The committed operation of a selection. Losing sends keep their values.
`closed` reports a send operation whose channel is closed: nothing was
sent, and the value stays with the caller (`select_keep` returns it).

### `SendError`

```lang
struct SendError<T> { pub value: T, pub reason: Symbol }
```

A failed send returns the unsent value.

#### `SendError.display`

```lang

```

### `batch`

```lang
fn batch<T>(options: BatchOptions) -> Result<BatchEndpoints<T>, ConfigError> where T: Transfer
```

Validate options and create a batch channel.

batch_defaults: {capacity: A, max_batch: B, byte_budget: C}
```

batch_policy: {discard_on_close: Bool, flush_latency: Duration}
```

### `batch_with_policy`

```lang
fn batch_with_policy<T>(options: BatchOptions, policy: BatchPolicy) -> Result<BatchEndpoints<T>, ConfigError> where T: Transfer
```

A batch channel with an explicit disposal/publication policy.

### `call`

```lang
fn call<Req, Resp>(to: Sender<Req>, request: fn(ReplySender<Resp>) -> Req) -> Option<Resp> !{Wait} where Req: Transfer, Resp: Transfer
```

Send a request made with a fresh reply sender and wait for the reply:
`none` if the request cannot be sent, or the replier closes the reply
sender without answering.

### `choose`

```lang
fn choose<R>(cases: List<Case<R>>, timeout: Option<Duration>) -> Option<R> !{Wait}
```

Heterogeneous selection: wait until one case commits (exactly one does;
ready cases rotate fairly) and return its mapped outcome, or `none` on
timeout. A send case whose channel is closed can never commit: it drops
out (an `on_send_keep` value goes back to `keep`), and when no case can
commit any more the result is `none`. Cases may receive and send different message types; the
outcomes meet in the caller's own type `R` (typically an enum).

### `create`

```lang
fn create<T>(options: Options) -> Result<Endpoints<T>, ConfigError> where T: Transfer
```

Validate options and create a prompt channel.

### `defaults`

```lang
defaults: {capacity: A, byte_budget: B}
```

### `on_recv`

```lang
fn on_recv<T, R>(r: Receiver<T>, f: fn(Option<T>) -> R) -> Case<R>
```

Receive from `r`; `f` gets the message, or `none` if the channel closed.

### `on_recv_batch`

```lang
fn on_recv_batch<T, R>(r: BatchReceiver<T>, f: fn(Option<T>) -> R) -> Case<R>
```

Receive one published message of batch channel `r`; `f` gets it, or
`none` if the channel closed and drained.

### `on_send`

```lang
fn on_send<T, R>(s: Sender<T>, value: T, f: fn() -> R) -> Case<R> where T: Share
```

Send `value` on `s`; `f` runs if this send commits. A losing shareable
payload is simply dropped; owned (affine) payloads use `on_send_keep`.

### `on_send_keep`

```lang
fn on_send_keep<T, R>(s: Sender<T>, value: T, f: fn() -> R, keep: fn(T) -> Unit) -> Case<R>
```

Like `on_send`, but if another case commits, `keep` receives the
unsent value back (its ownership is retained).

### `open`

```lang
fn open<T, R, E>(options: Options, body: fn(Endpoints<T>) -> Result<R, E>) -> Result<R, E> !{Wait} where E: From<ConfigError>, T: Transfer
```

Scoped prompt channel: closed when `body` ends (including on failure).

### `open_batch`

```lang
fn open_batch<T, R, E>(options: BatchOptions, body: fn(BatchEndpoints<T>) -> Result<R, E>) -> Result<R, E> !{Wait} where E: From<ConfigError>, T: Transfer
```

Scoped batch channel: staged messages are published and the channel is
closed when `body` ends.

### `reply`

```lang
fn reply<T>() -> ReplyEndpoints<T> where T: Transfer
```

A one-shot reply: the receiver waits for the single value the sender
sends (`call` passes the sender along with a request). Much cheaper than
a channel; sending twice is an error, and closing the sender without
sending makes the receiver's `recv` return `none`.

### `route`

```lang
fn route<T>(shards: List<Sender<T>>, key: Int) -> Sender<T>
```

The sender of shard `key` (any integer) among `shards`: requests for one
key always go to one shard, so a sharded actor serves them in order.

### `select`

```lang
fn select<T>(ops: List<Op<T>>, timeout: Option<Duration>) -> Selected<T> !{Wait} where T: Share
```

Wait for the first ready operation. Selection rotates fairly among ready
operations; use `select_priority` to prefer earlier ones explicitly.

### `select_keep`

```lang
fn select_keep<T>(ops: List<Op<T>>, timeout: Option<Duration>) -> (Selected<T>, List<T>) !{Wait}
```

Like `select`, but also returns the values of sends that did not
commit, in operation order: losing sends retain their ownership.

### `select_priority`

```lang
fn select_priority<T>(ops: List<Op<T>>, timeout: Option<Duration>) -> Selected<T> !{Wait} where T: Share
```

Like `select`, but when several operations are ready the earliest listed
one wins (explicit priority).
